subsystems.name: Collector swarm
subsystems.role: the inner layer — vast numbers of thin collectors that intercept starlight and turn it into power.

subsystems.name: Inner compute shell
subsystems.role: runs at the highest temperature the hardware allows, so its waste heat can still drive the layer outside it.

subsystems.name: Outer compute shells
subsystems.role: progressively cooler nested layers, each powered by the heat radiated by the one inside.

subsystems.name: Radiating surface
subsystems.role: the outermost layer — the only place the whole structure can dump its leftover heat to deep space.

subsystems.name: Materials and manufacturing system
subsystems.role: mines, refines and builds new structure from asteroids or dismantled planets.

subsystems.name: Control and workload layer
subsystems.role: decides what the machine actually computes, and how to keep a star-scale system fault-tolerant.

buildSteps.title: Choose a star and take inventory
buildSteps.detail: Select a single star with enough rocky material nearby — an asteroid belt or a planet that can be dismantled for metal, silicon and carbon.

buildSteps.title: Seed self-replicating industry
buildSteps.detail: Land a small number of mining and manufacturing units that build copies of themselves, growing output exponentially without further launches from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Capture the first light
buildSteps.detail: Produce the first thin collectors and place them close to the star, where sunlight is most intense — the beginning of a Dyson swarm.

buildSteps.title: Build the innermost shell
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a continuous computational layer at the highest temperature the materials tolerate, so its waste heat is still hot enough to be useful.

buildSteps.title: Nest the next shells outward
buildSteps.detail: Wrap further compute layers around the first, each running cooler on the heat radiated by the layer inside it.

buildSteps.title: Finish with radiators
buildSteps.detail: Cap the stack with the outermost shell, whose job is to reject the final, lukewarm heat into space at the lowest temperature achievable.

buildSteps.title: Rebalance and repair
buildSteps.detail: Continuously move collectors, replace failed elements and re-tune temperatures as the star evolves and workloads change.

buildSteps.title: Operate
buildSteps.detail: The completed structure converts essentially the entire stellar output into computation — the end state of a Kardashev Type II civilisation.

prerequisites.why: nothing today can grow its own industrial base from asteroid material; without it, building a star-scale structure is impossible.

prerequisites.tech: Extremely low-cost space launch and in-space assembly
prerequisites.why: the mass involved is astronomical; launch costs would have to fall by orders of magnitude.
every logical operation releases heat, so the total computation possible is bounded by how well that heat can be radiated away.
the outer layers can only work if they can radiate waste heat into the cold of space at very low temperature.
shells must survive micrometeoroids, radiation and thermal cycling for millions of years.

pathway.milestone: global data centres and orbital satellites
pathway.unlocks: experience in building and cooling very large distributed computing systems.

pathway.milestone: self-sufficient in-space manufacturing from asteroid material
pathway.unlocks: the ability to grow structure without launching it from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a partial Dyson swarm of independent solar collectors and computers
pathway.unlocks: capturing a small but growing fraction of a star's output.

pathway.milestone: nested shells at successively lower temperatures
pathway.unlocks: using nearly all stellar energy, not just the fraction a single layer can intercept.
computing capacity on a scale no planet-bound civilisation could approach.
